terminology.metadata_seal: A canonical SHA-256 over the complete checkpoint metadata object, excluding only metadata_sha256 itself.
terminology.integrity_not_authenticity: The seal detects accidental, incomplete, or coordinated metadata edits when the digest is not recomputed. It is not a MAC or signature and does not establish the author or truth of a checkpoint against an adversary able to recompute SHA-256.
terminology.progress_coverage: completed_steps, integrator counters, tensor records, restart metadata, compatibility identity, migration provenance, and every other registered metadata field are covered together.

new_writes: Every affected public writer emits only its newest sealed format.
The seal is computed after tensor-file records and every progress/restart field are final.
The published JSON contains exactly one lowercase metadata_sha256 value.
No solver state, equations, timestep order, tensor bytes, provider identity, production default, or Functional API version changes.
new_reads: Read format_version first through strict JSON parsing, then choose one exact version schema.
For a new format, verify metadata_sha256 before opening a tensor payload or mutating a target runtime.
A missing, malformed, or mismatched required seal raises CheckpointIntegrityError.
Unknown or missing keys remain fail-closed.
Tensor SHA-256, shape, dtype, finiteness, compatibility identity, and progress-consistency checks remain mandatory after the metadata seal passes.
legacy_reads: Released and already-supported v0.2 formats remain accepted by explicit version-specific read branches.
Legacy sources are never rewritten in place.
An unsealed legacy read cannot retroactively establish metadata integrity and must be reported as unsealed_legacy.
All frozen v0.2 fixtures must preserve their original tree hashes and pass state and one-step restart equivalence.
writer_boundary: The public writer rejects an object whose format_version is not the newest format.
Legacy bytes may be produced only by frozen fixtures or test-only helpers, not by a v0.3 production writer.
Explicit upgrades write a different target directory and never modify the source.
identity_boundary: Carrier format versions change; scientific and compatibility identities do not.
Provider identity and the Functional API version remain unchanged unless implementation evidence proves an unavoidable identity delta, in which case work stops for a separate decision.
The selected publication backend and integrity-observation status are not serialized into compatibility identity.

proposed_upgrade_surface.plane_format_2_to_3: non-in-place exact carrier upgrade after all existing v2 identity, progress, and tensor checks pass
proposed_upgrade_surface.legacy_channel_format_2_to_3: non-in-place exact carrier upgrade after all existing v2 dynamics, progress, and tensor checks pass
proposed_upgrade_surface.finite_q_format_1_to_2: non-in-place exact carrier upgrade after aggregate identity, component progress, and tensor checks pass
proposed_upgrade_surface.shadow_format_1_to_2: non-in-place experimental carrier upgrade after runtime, algebraic restart, progress, and tensor checks pass
proposed_upgrade_surface.integrity_claim: An upgrade seals the bytes and metadata it validated; it does not claim the unsigned source was historically authentic or untampered.

tamper_gate.required_result: Each mutation is rejected as CheckpointIntegrityError before payload loading, target mutation, timestep execution, or output-directory creation.
tamper_gate.negative_control: A pristine sealed checkpoint loads, restores, and advances identically to a continuous run.
tamper_gate.legacy_control: A frozen unsealed fixture remains readable under its exact legacy schema but is never described as digest verified.

qualification_plan.performance: No timestep-path code changes. Checkpoint I/O may hash one small JSON object once per write/read; this is outside timestep profiling.

decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A so A2-21 closes without leaving the same defect in a public pilot or packaged experimental writer.

decision_questions.question: May a v0.3 public writer emit an older unsealed format when passed a legacy checkpoint object?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A so every new v0.3 production write has the promised integrity seal.
